<!-- custom-release-notes:start -->
## Guardrails: verifier-config protection for every role, unconditional under `guardrails.enabled=false` (#3120)

`.secretscanignore` and every built-in verifier-config glob (`tsconfig*.json`,
`biome.json(c)`, `.eslintrc*`, `eslint.config.*`, `.prettierrc*`,
`prettier.config.*`, `oxlintrc*`, `.golangci*`) are now denied for **every
agent role** — including the OpenCode-native roles (`general`/`build`/`plan`/
`explore`) previously exempt from swarm write restrictions — and the denial
fires **even with `guardrails.enabled: false`** (and in observe contexts):
these files are owner policy for the verification system itself (the secretscan
Stage-A gate trusts `.secretscanignore`), so their integrity is not switchable
by the general enforcement knob. The shell path additionally routes no-scope
lenient roles through the verifier-config check (native-role `echo x >
.secretscanignore` via bash is blocked). Disclosed boundary: script runners
(`npm run <script>`, `bun run <script>`, `node <file>`) remain NOT treated as
shell write vectors — their targets are not statically knowable and blocking
them would break every legitimate build; see the `shell-write-detect` module
documentation.

## Shell write detection: patch, checkout-ref, rsync vectors (#3120)

`git apply` / `patch` (explicit `-p<n>`; both diff endpoints so a rename/delete
of a protected preimage cannot hide behind the postimage; closed option set —
`--directory`, `-d`, `-o`, `-r`, backup options, and index-writing modes
`--cached`/`--index`/`--3way` fail closed; `patch` without explicit `-p` fails
closed because GNU patch then picks basenames itself), `git checkout <ref>
<pathspec>…` (no `--`), and `rsync <src>… <dest>` are now detected as write
vectors and authorized per-target through the cd-tracking resolver. Targets
named inside a patch are extracted at authorization time from the patch file
(bounded read): tab- and space-prefixed `---/+++` headers, C-style octal
escapes (`\ooo` — accumulated as bytes and decoded once as UTF-8; unknown
escapes and undecodable sequences fail closed), all four quoted/unquoted
`diff --git` header combinations (git quotes each name independently
under its default `core.quotePath=true`), pure
rename sections (`rename from`/`rename to` — no `---/+++` lines), and
rename/delete endpoints that only exist as section headers. Patch targets
are judged under BOTH landings (git apply is patch-root-relative, GNU patch
is cwd-relative), and `rsync` also flags `--exclude`/`--include`/`--filter`
arguments as write paths. Unreadable/undecodable patches and stdin patches
block.

## PR_FEEDBACK: durably bound merge base + Stage A trust screens (#3396)

- PR_FEEDBACK activation resolves the merge base via ONE bounded `gh pr view`
  and durably binds `prFeedbackBaseRef/Sha` in gate state (fail-open: a
  resolution failure records `prFeedbackBaseBindingError` and never wedges
  activation; a failed binding is retried on the next matching re-activation
  and a successful re-resolution clears the stale advisory). The bound value
  is the real merge base (`git merge-base base_ref pr_head_sha`), not the
  base-branch tip, so callers whose base advanced keep trusted provenance.
  The `gh` subprocess runs BEFORE the checkout/session mutation locks so the
  network call never stalls concurrent gate mutations. Stage A verifies its
  caller-asserted `base_sha` against the binding: matching runs carry the
  root-level `prFeedbackStageABaseTrust: 'binding-verified'` verdict; a
  differing base ignores the caller provenance entirely (trusted
  base-identical scripts unavailable — identical to no-provenance) and
  persists a bounded `prFeedbackStageABaseMismatch` marker (durable-wins
  evidence, appended without advancing the gate revision, cleared by a head
  rebind). The receipt's strict child keeps the BASE two-value trust floor
  (rollback-safe: the 4-value verdict rides the passthrough-safe root field

# Erratum: v7.200.11 route-receipt hardening narrative

The v7.200.11 fragment described the #3380 fix's hardening layer with five
inaccurate claims. The delivered behavior (verified at the release commit and
re-verified by the 3509-3516 trace at `bf65b6efb`) is corrected below.

1. **Mis-attribution to the in-memory forget alone.** The fragment said "a
   failed persist now forgets the previous dispatch's in-memory route record
   for the task (a stale receipt could otherwise authorize the failed
   dispatch)". The forget was a no-op at its only call site: the dispatch
   whose persist failed never remembered a record (the persist failed first),
   so the slot's in-memory record always belonged to a PRIOR dispatch, and
   deleting the forget was proven suite-green by the #3516 mutation probes.
   What actually withheld the failed dispatch's settlement was the
   per-callID invalidation record — which the fragment omitted entirely. The
   follow-up PR (#3509/#3516) removes the dead forget and replaces the
   per-hook-instance invalidation map with a process-local registry.

2. **Omitted the `ROUTE_RECEIPT_INVALIDATED` settlement drop.** The fragment
   never mentioned that a settlement consult drops the failed dispatch's
   Stage-B settlement with the `route_blocked` reason class. That drop — and
   its enforcement half being unpinned by the shipped suite (the suite never
   called `toolAfter`) — is the subject of #3516 items 2, 3, and 8.

3. **Omitted the #3509 caveat.** The per-callID invalidation was recorded only
   when `routedTaskId` was already assigned. A routing fault BEFORE task
   resolution (including corrupt gate state that makes the routing block's
   raw read throw) recorded nothing, so a stale prior receipt could authorize
   exactly the dispatch the fix was meant to fence. #3509 tracks this; the
   follow-up PR records a whole-call fault marker for every pre-persist
   routing fault.

4. **False "proven at the settlement entry point".** The fragment claimed
   Stage-B fail-closure was "proven at the settlement entry point". The proof
   actually called `enforcePersistedReviewRouteReceipt` directly from the test
   — the REAL settlement call site (wired from
   `config.review_routing.enforce_receipts`) was never executed by the suite,
   and mutating the call site left the suite green (#3516 item 3). The
   follow-up PR pins the real call site through the real `toolAfter`
   settlement path.

5. **Stale "#3499 is being delivered" sentence.** PR #3499 had already merged
   before v7.200.11 was published; the sentence read as if the sibling work
   were still pending. It is deleted here.

The empty-binding-skip claim in the same fragment was accurate as written but
unpinned (deletable with the suite green); the follow-up PR pins it with a
leg whose removal reddens the suite. The capacity pre-flight claim ("a
capacity refusal can no longer burn the token") was overstated — the follow-up
PR pins the pre-flight with its own leg AND restates it as best-effort across
the reservation await: a concurrent dispatch admitted during the await can
still trip the remember-time capacity throw and burn the consumed token in
that window (the pre-flight narrows the window; it does not close it).

---

# `/swarm receipt --verify`: machine-checkable internal-consistency check for gate receipts on any machine (#2970, Workstream J slot J23)

`/swarm receipt --verify <bundle>` re-checks every recorded hash (receipt
hash, artifact digests, and the bundled gate report's re-derived digest) in
an exported receipt bundle on any machine — including a fresh clone with no `.swarm/`
state — and exits nonzero on any mismatch with a typed failure:
`corrupt_json`, `unsupported_format_version`, `schema_mismatch`,
`receipt_hash_mismatch`, `missing_artifact`, `digest_mismatch`, or
`path_escape`. The verify path is a pure function of the bundle's two roots
(receipt.json + artifacts/): no `.swarm/` reads, no config, no locks, zero
writes, and no child processes — which lets a reviewer mechanically reject
any bundle whose contents disagree with their own recorded hashes. It is
internal-consistency proof, not external attestation: a forger who
recomputes every digest consistently is only stopped by an out-of-band
capture-time anchor (a documented follow-up), and lazy edits that leave a
stale digest are caught because gate-report digests are RE-DERIVED from
the bundled bytes at verify time (FB-004). The same
classifier serves the `receipt` tool, so the tool's `ok` field and the
CLI's exit code can never disagree.

Path normalization and canonical hashing are imported from the emission
side (single source via `toPortableRelativePath` and the shared
canonicalizer), so a receipt emitted on Windows separators verifies
unchanged anywhere; `receipt_hash` covers the raw parsed object minus
`receipt_hash` itself, so an unknown added field flips verification
instead of being silently dropped.
The `--verify` arm accepts a bundle directory or a `receipt.json` path.

Documented limitations (inherited from the substrate): verify proves the
bundle is internally consistent and untampered relative to its recorded
hashes — it does not prove the cited gates ran against your clone's source
tree; an attached bundle contains the cited evidence artifacts even though
receipt JSON and verify output are digest-only; a future verifier that
re-executes cited commands would carry the full bounded-subprocess
obligation (AGENTS.md invariant 3) and needs its own issue.

---

# Verification receipts substrate: portable, hash-backed gate records (#2968, Workstream J slot J22)

`/swarm receipt <task|phase> <id>` and the new `receipt` tool emit a portable
record of the durably recorded gate outcomes for a task or phase: bounded gate records
(id, outcome, responsible actor, evidence refs — digests only, never raw
command output), the snapshot hashes the gates were evaluated against
(plan-structure / policy / phase-evidence), and content-hashed artifact refs.
Receipts land under `.swarm/evidence/receipts/` as canonical JSON
(`format_version 1.0.0`, `receipt_hash` computed over the raw parsed object minus `receipt_hash` itself)
plus rendered Markdown; `--export` writes a self-contained PR-attachable
bundle (receipt + Markdown + byte-copies of every cited artifact) under
`.swarm/plan-export/receipt-<kind>-<id>-<shorthash>/`. `--verify` ships in
this same release (see the `swarm-receipt-verify` fragment).

Behind the scenes: a phase's bounded gate report is durably captured at the
successful commit boundary (content-addressed write-once, fail-open to phase
completion — a receipt failure never fails a phase whose gates passed), the
derived receipts subtree is excluded from the phase-evidence snapshot so
emitting receipts can never mutate the identity the gates enforce, and the
new durable stream is registered in the observability retention registry
(mixed privacy; newest-8 per unit; staged atomic export; exported plan-export
bundles are reaped at close, completing the row's keyspace-bound claim).

Documented limitations: hash-only integrity is spoofable by a determined
local actor or by a model willing to recompute every digest consistently
— receipts s
